metadata.scope: 193 UN member states, the Holy See, Palestine, Kosovo and Taiwan; one marker per country entry.
metadata.attribution: Language reference adapted from Wikipedia contributors, List of official languages by country and territory, revision 1377657223 (CC BY-SA 4.0), with the linked country-specific corrections. Representative coordinates from Natural Earth 5.1.2 (public domain).
metadata.method: Country-level official designations are separated from de facto, working, national and regional designations. Regional lists reflect source coverage and are not a complete inventory of local laws. Country names and language designations are a reference, not detector support claims.

records.name: Argentina
notes: Argentine Sign Language is legally recognized; this is distinct from a nationwide official-language designation.

records.name: Brazil
regional: 95 municipalities and 3 Brazilian states have co-official languages, with 61 co-officialized languages. The list can be seen at Languages of Brazil.

records.name: Burkina Faso
notes: The constitutional designation covers national languages collectively, rather than an exhaustive named list.

records.name: Chile
regional: Languages of ethnic groups are official in their territories

records.name: Colombia
regional: Languages of ethnic groups are official in their territories

records.name: Ecuador
regional: Languages of ethnic groups are official in their territories

records.name: Eritrea
notes: No single official language is designated.

records.name: Ethiopia
notes: Federal working languages; regional governments designate their own languages.

records.name: Fiji
notes: The 2013 Constitution provides English, iTaukei and Hindi versions without declaring an official-language list.

records.name: Iceland
notes: Icelandic Sign Language has legal recognition and protections.

records.name: India
notes: Hindi and English are used for Union government purposes. State-level official languages are listed separately.

records.name: Kenya
notes: Kenyan Sign Language is also an official language of Parliament.

records.name: Mexico
notes: Spanish and Indigenous languages have national-language recognition; Spanish is shown here as de facto usage.

records.name: Netherlands
regional: English (in Sint Maarten, Sint Eustatius, Saba)

records.name: Niger
notes: The 2025 charter names Hausa as the national language and English and French as working languages.

records.name: Peru
regional: Quechua, Aymara and other native languages are official wherever they predominate.

records.name: Philippines
regional: Ilocano (in Luzon, official in La Union)

records.name: Spain
notes: Spanish is official nationwide; other languages have regional official status.

records.name: Switzerland
notes: Romansh is official in federal dealings with Romansh speakers.

records.name: United States
notes: English was designated the official language by executive order on March 1, 2025. State and territorial designations can differ.

records.name: Uruguay
notes: Uruguayan Sign Language is legally recognized.
